item.title: Lake Powell and Lake Mead water levels hit record lows
item.description: The water levels of Lakes Powell and Mead are at record lows. What does that mean for the millions of people who rely on the country's two biggest reservoirs and the Colorado River that feeds them?
item.content:encoded: The water levels of Lakes Powell and Mead are at record lows. What does that mean for the millions of people who rely on the country's two biggest reservoirs and the Colorado River that feeds them?
item.dc:creator: Ava Berger

item.title: Hurricane Lala strengthens as it heads to Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lala is headed toward Hawaii's Big Island. If it makes landfall there, it'd be the first hurricane to do so since 1871.
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Lala is headed toward Hawaii's Big Island. If it makes landfall there, it'd be the first hurricane to do so since 1871.

item.title: Families of USS Lincoln crew say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board
item.description: President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.

item.title: Trump administration wants to allow companies to hack foreign cybercriminals
item.description: The White House memorandum is thin on details, but it aims to give private businesses the ability to sabotage or spy on certain foreign actors.

item.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, is found dead
item.description: Arday was 37 when he became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023. He was found unresponsive Friday at a home in southwest London.

item.title: Should the U.S. have a mandatory retirement age?
item.description: Older workers are delaying retirement more and more. But it's causing younger workers to wonder if they're missing out on job advancement because senior roles aren't opening up. Is this true?

item.title: At Big Bend National Park, bulldozers begin clearing land for border barrier work
item.description: In the Big Bend area of West Texas, contractors are beginning to set the stage to build the Trump administration's planned border wall and barriers, despite bipartisan opposition.

item.title: No privacy, little downtime: Life aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Almost 5,000 sailors have spent months aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. As another carrier heads to relieve them, a former pilot takes us inside life on the ship.
